doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Violin, piano and the circus uncle who steered him to clarinet
summary: He started on violin and piano, but an uncle who played trombone with a circus told him to take a brass or reed instrument, so he took clarinet lessons from Manuel Rock.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: in music? Oh, no, when I was a small kid. My ambition was to play on a circuit. Yeah. My first
instrument was a violin. Oh. The next was a piano. Did you study those instruments? Yeah. But
I had an uncle that used to play with the old Hagenbeck-Wallace circus. The trombone, played trombone. And every year when the circus came to town, I wanted to go with him. And, uh, he
used to tell me, he says, well, uh, he says, man, he says, you can't go with the circus or playing a violin or a piano. He says, you don't care of those kind of instruments. You've got
to play a brass horn or drums or, or some kind of reed instrument, like a clarinet. So, I

settled for the clarinet. And, uh, like I said, this teacher of mine, uh, Manuel Rock, played in this band, Tooth Johnson's band, that, uh, Buddy Petit was in. I started taking lessons from him when I was about, uh, four and eleven years old. On clarinet? Yeah. And when I was about twelve years old, he used to take me on some of those gigs. Uh-huh.
